newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Biggest European brewer Heineken flat, fizz seen returning.
newsitem.headline: Biggest European brewer Heineken flat, fizz seen returning.

text.p: Heineken NV , Europe's biggest brewer, Friday announced a 1.4 percent dip in 1996 year profits but said it expected a recovery this year.
Net profit fell to 655 million guilders ($341 million) from 664 million ($346 million) in 1995, giving net per share of 13.06 guilders ($6.80) vs. 13.24 guilders ($6.90) per share.

Trading profit was little changed at 1.01 billion guilders ($526.3 million), while revenue, boosted by recent acquisitions, grew by 20 percent to 12.19 billion guilders ($6.4 billion) from 10.14 billion ($5.3 billion).
Heineken maintained its dividend at 3.50 guilders ($1.82) per share.
"A profit growth is expected for 1997. The amount of the profit growth cannot be predicted at the present moment," the company said in a statement.

"The figures are towards the upper range of expectations," said analyst Darrell Duthie at MeesPierson. "The outlook is interesting. Heineken is cautious and it looks as if it is trying to temper expectations somewhat."
Heineken said beer markets in Europe and North America would be "virtually stable" this year, while consumption in Asia and South America would show continued, albeit decreasing, growth.

Both the premium beer sector and sales of low-priced beers would become more important in these stable European markets, it said. Competition is becoming intense due to changes in distribution, a shift from the hotel, restaurant and cafe trade to buyers who drink at home, the concentration in the retail trade and the internationalization of the beer industry, it added.
All this was pressuring margins on standard beers, it said.

Heineken said it should benefit from a further rise in exports and lower raw material and packaging prices, but would remain vulnerable to a range of external factors -- currency moves, excise duties, political unrest, economic developments and the weather.
Heineken said that the world beer market grew by 1.4 percent in 1996, while total sales of beer brewed under its supervision rose by 10 percent and sales of Heineken branded beers rose 4.6 percent.
Heineken's Amstel brand maintained its sales volume in a declining segment market, while its Murphy's stout brand showed significant growth.
Heineken said its exports were a "particularly positive feature," growing by 10 percent in 1996.
Beer consumption fell in most parts of Europe, hit by moderate weather and weaker economies, but these lower sales were offset by gains in sales volumes in America and Asia.
